This long-term decline is further underscored by poor sales growth of only 4.96% over the past five years [E59]. The valuation of COSCO (India) Ltd presents a significant disconnect, as the stock trades at a P/E ratio of 80.5x [E1]. This high multiple is difficult to reconcile with the company’s long-term performance, specifically a compounded profit growth of -11% over the last decade and -26% over the last five years [E18, E19]. Furthermore, the company has failed to return capital to shareholders, evidenced by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Investors are also faced with a lack of top-line momentum, as the business has delivered poor sales growth of only 4.96% over the past five years [E59]. Conceded: [E6, E7, E8, E20, E21, E55, E63, E70]. While recent short-term growth figures show improvement, the historical trend of profit contraction and stagnant sales growth suggests that the current 80.5x earnings multiple may be unsupported by the company's underlying operational track record [E1, E18, E19, E59].
